audit.whatIsWrong: The chart is the generic Skill/Singed/Singed/Skill/Skill/Singed/Singed template and it contradicts the prose. whys[0] says Swain forces early HP leads, whys[1] says 'trading back requires standing in his root zone, which you cannot afford', whys[2] says he can 'root-bomb-poke you repeatedly with no reliable answer from your kit' — three straight Swain stages scored as even or Singed. Then level 6, which the mid paragraph calls the point where 'the matchup flips hard', is scored Skill.
audit.why: Emerald+ 55.80% over 767 games. Singed wins the matchup, but by surviving a genuinely losing first three levels and then never being catchable. The packet chart reads Swain, Swain, Swain, Skill, Singed, Singed, Singed, which is the prose exactly.
audit.corrected: Chart moved as one group to the packet read across both layers, with phases[0..4].why rewritten to match each new side.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Demonic Ascension as the spike that matters and never gives a cooldown for anything.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s and it is a drain that needs Swain standing next to you — against a champion who wins by running, it is the least relevant ability in his kit. The spike that actually decides the early lane is Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, and Vision of Empire at 22/21/20/19/18s is the one that punishes a proxy route. Insanity Potion is a flat 100s, so from 6 onward your ult is up more often than his.
audit.corrected: focus, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], phases[3].why and phases[4].why rebuilt around Nevermove's 12s, Vision of Empire's 22s and the two ult cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. First, Nevermove is described wrongly everywhere it appears: 'he throws it from range, roots you on the spot' in early, 'Swain's E pull is ranged and roots on contact' in whys[0], 'Land E to root you inside W slow-bomb' in wants.foe[0]. Second, the single most important interaction in this matchup is nowhere on the page — Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds. The packet also flags that Swain's abilities are never named at all.
audit.why: Riot's Nevermove text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the return pass, not the throw. That single fact changes how you walk: you sidestep twice, and the safe move after the wave passes you is to keep going rather than to stop. Meanwhile Riot's Insanity Potion text says it makes 'his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds' — and Swain's entire kit is healing: Ravenous Flock soul fragments heal him and permanently raise his max health, and Demonic Ascension is a drain. Halving all of that for 100 seconds is the reason Singed wins this lane, and it is not written anywhere.
audit.corrected: early, whys[0], whys[4], wants.you[1], wants.foe[1], dosFull[0], dosFull[1].t, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1] and report[5].t. Every Swain ability is now named.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] is titled 'Build MR + anti-heal' as if anti-heal were something you must buy.
audit.why: You already own it. Insanity Potion turns Poison Trail into a Grievous Wounds applicator for its full 100s, which is a shorter cooldown than his 120s ult. Buying a second source is optional; knowing the first exists is not.

edits.before: Swain's E pull is the whole early game — he throws it from range, roots you on the spot, drops W under your feet, and Q pokes while you stand in the slow. Do not give him a stationary target: hug the minion wave so E clips a creep instead of you, and never run at him in a straight line before level 6. If he burns E on the wave, that is your window to shove and proxy behind his tower; he cannot engage you without it and his Q damage alone is not enough to stop a healthy Singed from farming through the back line.
edits.after: Nevermove is the whole early game, and it does not root on the throw — the wave travels out, turns, and returns to Swain, and the root lands on the way home. Sidestep both halves. Hug the minion wave so it clips a creep instead of you, and never walk at him in a straight line before level 6. Once he has spent it, 12 seconds at rank 1 is your window to shove and proxy behind his tower: Death's Hand chip alone will not stop a healthy Singed farming through the back line.

notes: Vision of Empire is worth a second pass that would not fit here: it is 5500 range at rank 1 rising to 7500, reveals the champion it hits, and gives Swain a Soul Fragment — so a Singed running a fixed proxy route can be tagged and revealed from across the map without Swain leaving his lane. Only the 22s cooldown made it into breakdown.cooldowns. Also left alone: content mid, late and whys[6] all still call his abilities E/W/R rather than by name, which the packet flags as a defect; each would need a full-paragraph rewrite to fix and I prioritised the Nevermove and Grievous Wounds corrections instead.
